question: According to the sign convention for lenses, all distances measured in the direction of incident light are taken as:

options.text: depends on the type of lens

solution:
The correct answer is __**positive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **optical center (O)** of the lens is treated as the **origin**, and the **principal axis** of the lens is taken as the **X-axis** of the coordinate system.
 
• All distances measured in the **direction of incident light** (usually from left to right) are taken as **positive**. ***Hence, the correct answer is positive.***
 
• Conversely, all distances measured in the direction **opposite to the direction of incident light** are taken as **negative**.
 
• The **object** is always placed to the **left** of the lens, which implies that the **incident light** moves from **left to right**.
 
• Distances measured **perpendicular to and above** the **principal axis** (upward) are taken as **positive**.
 
• Distances measured **perpendicular to and below** the **principal axis** (downward) are taken as **negative**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Object Distance (u):** Since the **object** is always placed on the **left** side of the lens, the **object distance (u)** is always **negative** according to the sign convention.
 
• **Focal Length (f):**
 
 
• The **focal length** of a **convex lens** (converging lens) is always **positive** because its **principal focus** lies on the **right side** of the optical center.
 
• The **focal length** of a **concave lens** (diverging lens) is always **negative** because its **principal focus** lies on the **left side** of the optical center.
 
 
 
• **Image Distance (v):**
 
 
• For a **real image**, which is formed on the **right side** of the lens, the **image distance (v)** is **positive**.
 
• For a **virtual image**, which is formed on the **left side** (same side as the object), the **image distance (v)** is **negative**.
 
 
 
• **Magnification (m):** This is the ratio of the **height of the image (h')** to the **height of the object (h)**.
 
 
• If **magnification** is **negative**, the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• If **magnification** is **positive**, the image is **virtual and erect**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula:** The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula: **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**. It is vital to apply the correct signs to these values before calculation.
 
• **Power of a Lens (P):** The **power of a lens** is defined as the reciprocal of its **focal length** in **meters** (**P = 1/f**).
 
 
• The **SI unit** of power is **Dioptre (D)**.
 
• A **convex lens** has **positive power**, while a **concave lens** has **negative power**.
 
 
 
• **Height Convention:** The **height of the object (h)** is usually taken as **positive** as it is placed **above** the principal axis. The **height of the image (h')** is **positive** for **virtual images** and **negative** for **real images**.
 
• **Optical Center:** It is the **central point** of a lens. A ray of light passing through the **optical center** emerges without any **deviation**.
